passages.text: When you’ve seen pleasant sights and unpleasant ones, too, dispel all manner of desire for the pleasant, without hating what you don’t like.
passages.note: Equanimity toward the pleasant and unpleasant

passages.text: When you’ve smelled a pleasant, fragrant scent, and one that’s foul and unpleasant, dispel aversion for the unpleasant, while not yielding to desire for the pleasant. When you’ve enjoyed a sweet, delicious taste, and sometimes those that are bitter, don’t be attached to enjoying sweet tastes, and don’t despise the bitter.
passages.note: Accepting life's bitter and sweet without clinging
